It initializes from random Gaussian packets and upsamples by i…

This program optimizes a Dinkelbach-style surrogate (smooth-max minus λ·num) with L-BFGS-B gradients on a fixed grid, rather than the record's approach of building a tuned small-n construction and carefully upsampling it. It grows resolution by repeat-upsampling through a fixed stage ladder (64→2048) with per-stage time shares, whereas the record avoided interpolation because it destroys tuned st…

axes.name: How is a candidate solution represented?

values.name: a dense real-valued array of samples on a fixed uniform grid (default length 50)
a parametric analytic form (e.g. Gaussian, triangle, piecewise polynomial) with few parameters
a sparse / low-degree representation (e.g. Fourier coefficients or a few basis-function weights)
Raw nonnegative knot values on a uniform grid, renormalized to sum 1 after each step
Low-dimensional basis: spline/B-spline coefficients or Fourier/Chebyshev modes
Softmax/log-parameterization (f = exp(g)/sum exp(g)) to enforce positivity and normalization intrinsically

axes.name: How is the first solution built?

values.name: constant ones (or the externally supplied start unchanged)
random smooth function (e.g. low-frequency random Fourier series)
a hand-designed bump/indicator-like shape
Random Gaussian packet mixture (8 bumps with random positions/widths) at the coarsest grid, seeded by a fixed RNG
Deterministic analytic seeds: single bump, uniform, or known Boyer-Li / Jaech-Joseph constructions
Multi-start portfolio of diverse structured seeds (comb, two-bump, staircase) with best-of selection

axes.name: What quantity does the search optimise while it runs?
Which moves or update steps change a solution?

values.name: no search at all: return the provided start or a fixed constant
local gradient-free search (coordinate/pattern search, simulated annealing) on the samples
population-based evolutionary search over parameters or samples

axes.name: How does the search accept worse solutions or escape a local optimum?

values.name: accept slightly worse with small probability
no acceptance of worse; restart on stall

axes.name: How is the problem's scale handled (all at once, coarse to fine, in parts)?

values.name: Fixed geometric ladder of grid sizes (64 up to 2048/4096) with hand-tuned per-stage time shares, upsample by linear interpolation between stages
Single fixed high resolution from the start (no ladder, no interpolation)
Adaptive resolution: refine grid only when the optimizer stalls, with structure-preserving (spline/Fourier) upsampling

axes.name: Which parts, if any, are solved exactly?
How is the time budget split between phases?

values.name: ignores budget_seconds entirely
run iterative optimization until budget_seconds elapses
allocate budget to a coarse-to-fine multi-resolution refinement
Static pre-assigned fraction of the budget per stage, plus a final polish stage at high beta
Adaptive budget: allocate time proportional to observed improvement rate per stage
Single global time budget with early stopping when marginal gain falls below a threshold

axes.name: How is the ratio R optimised: the objective the optimiser actually works on

values.name: Dinkelbach: maximise ||f*f||_2^2 - lambda*||f*f||_1*smoothmax(f*f), then lambda = R, repeated
Gradient steps on R itself (or log R) with a smooth max
Active-set minimax: the tied maxima of f*f as constraints with dual weights (LP, SLSQP, persistent dual)
Exact line search on R per block or run of f (no gradient)
Alternating projection: push f*f towards a two-level target, then project back to f >= 0
Dinkelbach-style: fix lambda = current exact R, minimize (surrogate sup) - lambda*(num), update lambda from exact R each round
Directly maximize the exact ratio R(f) with a single nonconvex objective and its analytic gradient
Alternating/parametric: bisect on a target ratio t and test feasibility of sup - t*num <= 0

axes.name: How is the maximum of f*f (the L-infinity norm) handled in the optimised objective

values.name: Exact maximum (a subgradient at the arg max)
LogSumExp smooth max normalised by max(f*f), beta annealed upward (1e5 to 1e9 and beyond, up to 1e14)
A fixed mild smooth max (beta about 100-500 relative to the max)
A softmax- or p-norm-weighted set of the top lags
Smooth log-sum-exp (soft-max) surrogate of ||f*f||_inf with an annealed sharpness beta, inside a Dinkelbach/ratio loop
Exact piecewise-linear knot objective with subgradient or bundle method (no smoothing)

axes.name: Which local optimiser solves the inner problem

values.name: L-BFGS on the smooth surrogate, many iterations per Dinkelbach round
L-BFGS with Anderson acceleration of the Dinkelbach iterates
Adam with gradient noise and elitist respawn of the worst candidates
Simulated annealing or random search on f
gradient ascent with momentum and adaptive line search
L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients and nonnegativity bounds, restarted in a loop until the time budget expires
Projected gradient / FISTA with momentum and adaptive step
Trust-region or interior-point Newton on a reduced parameterization (e.g. softmax or spline coefficients)

axes.name: How is f >= 0 enforced

values.name: f = w^2 exactly (a cell at zero stays at zero: the support is locked)
Clip or project to f >= 0 after each step
An explicit support mask pruned on purpose (zero the smallest cells, re-optimise, repeat)
none imposed; f is unconstrained and scale-invariant ratio is relied on
fix ||f||_1 or ||f||_2 to a constant to remove scale freedom
restrict f to be nonnegative

axes.name: How is the number of steps n chosen and changed

values.name: Exact k-fold repeat np.repeat(f, k) (R unchanged), then polish at the finer grid
Zero-pad to the step limit and polish there, letting structure grow into the padding
Average-pool a finer construction down to n, then polish (a basin transplant)
Coarse to fine, upsampling by interpolation between stages

axes.name: What is the macro shape (the envelope) of f across its domain

values.name: One heavy comb block holding about 30% of the mass at one end, an empty gap beside it, a graded ramp of bumps
A tall spike plus a comb of smaller peaks
A smooth arcsine-like density, 1/sqrt(1 - 4x^2) on [-1/2, 1/2]
A parametric series sum_j a_j (1 - 4x^2)^(j - 1/2) (about 100 terms)
Regular sparse packets under a smooth raised-cosine envelope

axes.name: What is the fine structure of f (the comb of teeth or blocks)

values.name: A fine, coherent periodic lattice of teeth (period about 0.3% of the domain)
Contiguous blocks with irregular spacing found by optimisation (hundreds to thousands of blocks)
A coarser parent with each cell split into about 20 sub-cells under a phase kernel
Number-theoretic support (Sidon/B2 sets, difference sets, quadratic residues)
Regular [small, big, small] triplets

axes.name: Once converged, how does the program try to leave the local optimum

values.name: Small noise (about 1e-8 x max f), then a full re-polish, with momentum along the last improving step
Perturb along the gradient of the transition loss (lags where f*f crosses between its levels), re-polish
Perturb only the lowest 1-5% Fourier modes of f, then re-polish
Structural surgery on blocks (shift, scale, split, merge, remove), then re-polish
Exact single-coordinate moves on the tied plateau (incremental update of f*f, no FFT)

axes.name: Which part of f*f does the program's step aim at

values.name: The level transitions of f*f (lags with f*f/max between 0.1 and 0.9)
Only the tied maxima (the active set of the L-infinity norm)
Small-mass runs of f first

axes.name: How is the objective (the convolution and its norms) computed numerically?

values.name: compute f*f by direct convolution on the sampled grid, then take discrete L2, L1, Linf norms of the convolution
evaluate the ratio analytically for a parametric family
use FFT-based convolution with careful normalization and boundary handling

axes.name: What domain and boundary treatment is used for the convolution?

values.name: finite interval with zero-padding implied by discrete convolution, no explicit boundary policy
periodic (circular) convolution on a torus
explicit zero extension with a chosen support width

axes.name: What symmetry or shape assumptions are imposed on f?

values.name: general unconstrained shape, no symmetry enforced
enforce even symmetry (f(x)=f(-x))
enforce a unimodal or compactly supported shape

axes.name: Is there a separate final high-precision polish pass (larger beta, tighter tolerances, or exact-knot local search) after the main run?

values.name: A separate polish pass at the largest grid with much larger beta_max (1e7) and tighter tolerances
No separate polish; keep one beta schedule throughout
Post-hoc exact-knot local search (coordinate/subgradient descent on the piecewise-linear R) to squeeze the last digits
